title: Mid Module Feedback
html:
Published: 2026-11-02T11:25:52.284Z

Hi everyone,


Thank you for submitting your feedback for the Advanced Web Development module. We appreciate you taking the time to share your thoughts. Based on the specific comments raised, here is how we are addressing them:


  1. Fast Pacing and Steep Learning Curve: A couple of you noted that the module moves very fast and feels compressed. As highlighted at the start of term, this is the nature of full-stack development: industry-standard frameworks require an intensive pace, backed by substantial self-learning and independent practice outside of class. While demanding, this exposure is designed to give you a solid foundation in the modern workflows and problem-solving skills expected in industry.
  2. Lecture Slides and Dense Code: You mentioned that the lectures contain a huge number of slides with dense code, making it difficult to keep up or digest the material. The code shown on the slides was meant to provide you with solutions. Moving forward: We will adjust the lecture structure to focus on the theory and the "why" behind the implementations first, followed by the code. We will slow the pace down and cut down the amount of code directly on the slides, providing the full code as reference files instead.
  3. Lectures Running into Lab Time: A comment noted that lectures occasionally run over into lab time. We will stick strictly to the scheduled finish time for the lecture to ensure you have the full lab duration.
  4. Lab Sheets ("Do X, Now Do Y") and Working Through Gaps: Feedback mentioned that the lab sheets focus on step-by-step actions without in-depth explanations of every line, and that encountering gaps can leave you stuck. This structure is intentional. In web development, tasks are rarely plain sailing, and learning how to work through ambiguities is an essential practical skill. As advised at the start of the module, you are encouraged to use AI tools when you get stuck to explain concepts, troubleshoot errors, and bridge gaps as part of your active learning process. The teaching team is also on hand during labs to assist when you hit a wall.
  5. Readiness for Coursework Projects: Some of you shared that you do not feel ready to start your projects and worry about relying solely on lab code. Bridging lab examples into independent project work requires actively exploring and understanding how the code functions. When you encounter ambiguity or are unsure how to adapt a pattern, be proactive: consult AI tools to break down unfamiliar code, test modifications, and make full use of the ATs available during lab hours to ask questions. Engaging with these resources directly is essential for meeting the learning outcomes and gaining the confidence needed for your coursework.

Thank you again for your time and providing us your feedback, we really appreciate it.


Jeannette and the Teaching Team

title: Week 7: Introduction to WebAI with TensorFlow.js
path: Announcements/Week 7: Introduction to WebAI with TensorFlow.js
html:
Published: 2026-10-30T09:00:06.966Z

Hello everyone,


I hope your work on Coursework 001 is going well.


From Week 7, we will begin the second half of the module, focusing on WebAI. The ability to integrate AI models and features into web applications is becoming an increasingly valuable skill for modern web developers.


Our first WebAI lecture will take place on Tuesday, 3 November, from 14:00 to 16:00 in the Data Science and AI Lab (Sci 0.59).


This session will introduce the foundations of WebAI using Google’s TensorFlow.js. It will prepare you for the following weeks, when we will explore pretrained models, WebAI applications and bounded AI-agent features.


I appreciate that many of you will be busy completing Coursework 001. However, I strongly recommend attending this lecture because it establishes the key concepts needed for the rest of the module and Coursework 002.


The lecture will be followed by a practical lab from 16:00 to 18:00 in the same room. Weekly lecture slides, lab exercises and assessment information will be posted on Blackboard. Please review the materials before each lecture and lab where possible.


If you have any questions about the second half of the module, please contact me at Cheng.C.Wang@uea.ac.uk.


We look forward to seeing you next week.


Cheng and the Teaching Team

It was great seeing you all in class on Tuesday. I hope you are making good progress on this week's lab exercises. Have a productive week and see you all next week!

title: Week 3
html:
Published: 2026-10-07T07:56:20.529Z

Hi everyone,


It was great seeing you all in yesterday's Advanced Web Development class, and a big thank you to those who took the time to share feedback - it is always appreciated.


As mentioned at the start of the semester, this module moves at a brisk pace. We have a lot of ground to cover, which makes independent study outside of class essential. Please make sure to stay on top of the learning materials and complete your lab exercises before next week’s session. If you run into any blockers or have questions while working through them, don't hesitate to reach out.


Looking ahead to next week, we will be diving into Web Security with Open Authorisation (Auth0 API) & Prisma ORM. In this session, we will focus on hands-on implementation, including:


  • Setting up authentication using the Google Provider via Auth0
  • Integrating our application database using Prisma ORM

Have a productive week and see you all next week!


Jeannette and the Teaching Team

path: Announcements/Week 2: Lab Fixes, Git Reminders, and Looking Ahead to Next Week
html:
Published: 2026-09-30T07:50:13.126Z

Hello students,


It was great seeing everyone in class yesterday! Thank you all for your engagement.


Here are a few important updates and reminders for this week:


  1. VS Code "JSON to TS" Extension: We are aware that the JSON to TS plugin is currently unavailable on the lab machines; apologies for the inconvenience. To work around this, I have uploaded the required TypeScript types (BookProps.tsx) directly to Blackboard. Please download this file and place it into the appropriate folder in your project.
  2. Lab Progress (Lab 2.0 & 2.1): Well done to everyone who finished Lab 2.0 during the session! I strongly encourage you to complete Lab2.1 before next week’s class. This part focuses on working with simple React state, which will be essential moving forward.
  3. Use StuGit, Not Personal GitHub: A quick reminder that all coursework and lab repositories for this module must be hosted on our internal StuGit instance, not your personal GitHub accounts.
  4. Lecture Code: If you want to review or build on the code demonstrated in yesterday's lecture, the repository URLs can be found directly in the lecture slides on Blackboard.

Looking Ahead to Next Week


Next week we dive into Next.js and Redux Toolkit (RTK). We will cover:


  • Next.js Basics & Rendering Strategies
  • Routing and Navigation
  • Client vs. Server Components
  • Data Fetching (Client and Server)
  • The useEffect hook
  • Global State Management with Redux Toolkit

See you all in the next week!



Jeannette and the Teaching Team

title: Week 1
html:
Published: 2026-09-23T08:08:48.887Z

Hi everyone,


It was great meeting you all yesterday for our first sessions of the module! I hope you found the induction informative and that the introduction to TypeScript provided a solid foundation for what is ahead.


Please take note of the following key reminders and updates for the week:

  • Week 1 Lab Exercises: Ensure you complete the TypeScript lab exercises before our next lecture. Consistent hands-on practice is essential for keeping up with the coursework.
  • Git Repository Support: If you encounter any difficulties accessing or configuring your student Git repository, please reach out to the teaching team as soon as possible so we can get it sorted.
  • Assignment 001 Released: Assignment 001 has been released on BB. Please note that this is an individual assessment. Take time to read through the specification thoroughly. If anything requires clarification, post your questions on the discussions board or email me; I will address common queries at the start of next week's session.
  • Looking Ahead to Week 2 (React): Next week, we will dive into React, web frontend development. Please review the preparatory learning materials and readings uploaded under the Week 2 folder on the BB before next week session so you can get the most out of the lecture.

Have a productive week, and we look forward to seeing you all in the next session!



Jeannette and the Teaching Team

title: Welcome to the module
html:
Published: 2026-09-18T08:00:51.105Z

Hello everyone,


I hope you all had a restful summer break. Welcome back!


This module is designed to take your web development skills to the next level. To succeed, you'll need to be proficient in JavaScript, especially with functions and asynchronous programming concepts (Promise, async and await).


Over the semester, we'll dive into two main topics:


  • First, you'll learn to build modern full-stack web applications using the latest version of Next.js and React.
  • Then, we'll explore WebAI, exploring TensorFlow.js & Transformers.js to run models directly on the browser.

Our first lecture is scheduled for Tuesday, 22 September, from 14:00 - 16:00 in Data Science and AI Lab (room Sci 0.59). During this session, I will introduce the module, provide details about the first assessment, and then we'll dive in our full stack web development starts with Typescript. Your attendance is important, as we will cover key information.


The lecture will be followed by a practical lab session from 16:00 to 18:00 in the same lab.


All module materials, including weekly lecture slides, lab exercises, and assessment details, will be posted on the Blackboard module page in a timely manner. Please take some time to review these materials before each week's lecture and lab.


If you have any questions, please don't hesitate to reach out to me at j.chin@uea.ac.uk.


We look forward to seeing you all next week!



Jeannette and the Teaching Team
